concept: merge combines DataFrames using keys. Missing values require deliberate handling: a missing metric is not always zero.
example:
import pandas as pd
customers = pd.DataFrame({"customer": [1, 2, 3]})
orders = pd.DataFrame({"customer": [1, 1, 2], "amount": [500, 300, 600]})
revenue = orders.groupby("customer", as_index=False)["amount"].sum()
result = customers.merge(revenue, on="customer", how="left")
result["amount"] = result["amount"].fillna(0)
breakdown: Group orders first so revenue has one row per customer.
The unmatched customer gets NaN revenue.
fillna(0) is appropriate only because the business definition treats no orders as zero revenue.
practice: Add an order_count column to revenue before merging, then fill missing revenue and count with zero.
answer:
revenue = orders.groupby("customer", as_index=False).agg(
    amount=("amount", "sum"), order_count=("amount", "size"))
result = customers.merge(revenue, on="customer", how="left")
result[["amount", "order_count"]] = result[["amount", "order_count"]].fillna(0)
takeaways: Validate merge cardinality to avoid duplicated metrics.
Missing, unknown, and zero can mean different things.
